'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Al-Shifa Hospital siege]]
***A third [[mass grave]] holding at least 49 bodies is discovered in [[Gaza City]]'s [[al-Shifa Hospital]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/5/8/israels-war-on-gaza-live-calls-for-israel-to-open-border-crossings-grow (Al Jazeera)] [https://thehill.com/policy/international/4652018-reports-mount-of-mass-graves-at-gaza-hospitals-some-without-heads/ (The Hill)]
**[[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[Israel]] reopens the [[Kerem Shalom border crossing]], allowing humanitarian aid into [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. However, the [[UN]] states that no aid has entered. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-war-news-05-08-2024-495e6dabfdddc5587bd20e71b6ad421d (AP)]
**[[Rafah offensive]]
***[[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli troops]] reach the outskirts of [[Rafah]] with [[Hamas]] saying that heavy fighting is underway. The Israeli military says that it has "uncovered terrorist infrastructure" and killed a number of Hamas militants as it advances. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-68975398 (BBC News)]
*[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**Two Hezbollah and three PIJ killed in Israeli airstrikes in [[southern Lebanon]].[https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hezbollah-trade-heavy-fire-violence-escalates-2024-05-08/ (Reuters)] 
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***Russia launches [[missile]] and [[Drone warfare|drone strikes]] across [[Ukraine]], injuring three people and damaging [[critical infrastructure]]. Ukraine says that it shot down 39 of 55 missiles and 20 of 21 drones. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-5-8-2024-e4b4507e3f17965a8ad69fdfb8dfa48d (AP)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-08/ukraine-s-kyiv-lviv-under-attack-after-more-than-1-month-pause (Bloomberg News)]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]]
***At least seven people, including four children, are injured in a [[Russia]]n [[airstrike]] on [[Kharkiv]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-attack-hits-school-stadium-injures-four-children-ukraines-kharkiv-2024-05-08/ (Reuters)]
**Russia occupies the villages of [[Novokalynove]] in Donetsk Oblast and [[Kyslivka, Kharkiv Oblast|Kyslivka]] in Kharkiv Oblast. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/russia-claims-to-have-taken-control-of-2-ukrainian-settlements/3213821 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
**A motorcycle bombing kills three [[Taliban]] security personnel in [[Badakhshan Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. The [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/blast-north-afghanistan-kills-three-taliban-security-personnel-2024-05-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Tornadoes of 2024]]
**[[Tornado outbreak of May 6–8, 2024]]
***Dozens of tornadoes strike the United States over the past three days, killing five people and leaving multiple others injured. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/08/us/tornadoes-storms-missouri-illinois-tennessee.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods]]
**The death toll from the ongoing heavy flooding in southern [[Brazil]] increases to 100, with 128 people still missing and 163,000 people displaced. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/death-toll-heavy-rains-brazil-hits-100-2024-05-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Rolling blackouts]] occur in several cities in [[Mexico]] amid an ongoing [[heatwave]] in the country. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/08/world/americas/mexico-blackout-heat-wave.html (''The New York Times'')]
*A [[Boeing 767]] operated by [[FedEx]] is forced to make an emergency landing at [[Istanbul Airport]] after the front [[landing gear]] fails to deploy. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/article/2024/may/08/boeing-cargo-plane-forced-to-land-at-istanbul-without-front-landing-gear (''The Guardian'')]
*A [[Republic of Singapore Air Force]] (RSAF) [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16C]] fighter jet crashed at [[Tengah Air Base]] after the pilot experienced issues during take-off. The pilot ejected successfully and is receiving medical attention. The RSAF has temporarily suspended training for the F-16 fleet until investigations show that it is safe to resume. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/rsaf-f-16-crashes-at-tengah-airbase-pilot-safe (''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.mindef.gov.sg/web/portal/mindef/news-and-events/latest-releases/article-detail/2024/May/09may24_nr2 (''MINDEF Singapore'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
**[[AstraZeneca]] withdraws its marketing authorizations in [[Europe]] and withdraws its [[COVID-19]] [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccines]] worldwide due to low demand, after finding that the vaccines can very rarely lead to blood clots. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2024/05/07/astrazeneca-withdrawing-covid-vaccine/ (''The Telegraph'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Human trafficking in India]]
**The [[India]]n [[Central Bureau of Investigation]] arrests four people linked to a network of human traffickers who have been luring young men to go to Russia with the promise of jobs or university admission, then forcing them to fight in the [[Russo-Ukrainian War|war in Ukraine]]. The [[Ministry of External Affairs (India)|Ministry of External Affairs]] is working with [[Russia]] to secure discharges for 20 Indian nationals in the [[Russian Army]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/8/india-arrests-four-for-duping-young-men-into-fighting-for-russia-in-ukraine (Al Jazeera)]
*Two [[Cambodia]]n and [[China|Chinese]] people are deported from [[Singapore]] after being convicted of laundering over [[Singapore dollar|S$]]3 billion (US$2.2 billion), Singapore's largest ever [[money laundering]] case. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/crime/cambodian-chinese-deported-from-singapore-in-historic-money-laundering-4743671.html (''VnExpress'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[List of elected British politicians who have changed party affiliation|Elected British politicians who have changed party affiliation]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] MP [[Natalie Elphicke]] [[Party switching|defects]] to the opposition [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], citing the [[Sunak ministry|Sunak government]]'s failure to stop the [[English Channel migrant crossings (2018–present)|English Channel migrant crisis]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/another-british-conservative-lawmaker-defects-opposition-labour-party-2024-05-08/ (Reuters)]
*The [[United States House of Representatives]] vote 359–43 to keep [[Mike Johnson (Louisiana politician)|Mike Johnson]] as [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]], defeating an initiative by [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]] to have him removed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/9/us-house-blocks-bid-to-remove-speaker-mike-johnson (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*Researchers at [[Google DeepMind]] announce the development of [[AlphaFold|AlphaFold 3]], an AI model that can predict the structures of almost all biological molecules and model the interactions between them. [https://time.com/6975934/google-deepmind-alphafold-3-ai/ (''Time'')] [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07487-w (''Nature'')]
